name: Vile Familiars
summary: Near the Den, Vile Familiars threaten warlocks who seek the power of demons. Ruzan asks you to prove your strength by bringing back their heads. This is the first dangerous step toward mastering fel power under the Horde’s watchful eyes.

sections.title: A Precarious Place in the Horde
sections.body: Warlocks have an uneasy place in Thrall’s new Horde. Demonic corruption and blood pacts once brought ruin to the orcs, leaving deep scars and distrust. Durotar tolerates fel magic, but its practitioners are neither loved nor welcomed. Many warlocks live apart and practice in shadowed places like the Den, away from prying eyes. There, they teach the few initiates daring enough to follow their path.

sections.title: The Trial of Mastery
sections.body: Ruzan asks you to prove your strength before he teaches you the dangerous rites for bending an imp to your will. Vile Familiars lurk near a cave northeast of the Den and hurl bolts of flame at those who approach. Slay these lesser demons and bring their heads back to Ruzan. They will show him you can overcome the fiery creatures you hope to control. Only then can you face the danger of the magic you seek to command.

faq.q: Why does Ruzan send warlocks to fight vile familiars?
faq.answer: Ruzan sends you to face an imp’s fiery nature and danger before you try to summon one. Warlocks are few and distrusted, so he asks you to prove you can defeat such creatures before teaching you demon summoning.

faq.q: Where are the vile familiars found?
faq.answer: Vile Familiars gather around and inside a cave northeast of the Den in the Valley of Trials, beyond the roaming boars and scorpids. The cave is an encampment for the Burning Blade Coven.

faq.q: How does the Horde view warlocks in Durotar?
faq.answer: Warlocks face deep suspicion across the Horde because demonic corruption once scarred the orcs. Thrall’s government tolerates them and sees their value in battle, yet many still live apart.

faq.q: What reward does completing this trial offer?
faq.answer: Bringing Ruzan the heads of slain Vile Familiars proves you have the strength and discipline to command demons. He can then teach you to summon an imp minion.
Yes. Vile Familiars are minor demonic imps tied to fel magic. Though small, they are formidable foes who hurl fireballs at their enemies.
Ruzan is an orc warlock trainer in the Den in the Valley of Trials. He teaches new orc warlocks to harness fel energy safely and control summoned servants.

angles.text: As a warlock, you face this first trial to prove you can subdue demonic fire before learning the rite to summon an imp of your own.
As an orc, you meet your people’s dark history each day. You must prove your control and loyalty in a society that remembers the horrors of fel corruption.
As a member of the Horde, you can train as a warlock in Durotar, though the dark arts remain confined to isolated places like the Den.
